item.title: 'Guns-a-blazing': Donald Trump threatens US military action in Nigeria, vows to halt aid over Christian killings
item.description: Former US President Donald Trump has threatened military intervention and aid cuts to Nigeria, citing the alleged killing of Christians. He instructed the Department of War to prepare for action, warning the Nigerian government to act swiftly.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Intentional' explosion hits Harvard Medical School; police release suspects' photos
item.description: An early Saturday morning explosion at Harvard Medical School's Goldenson Building has been deemed 'intentional' by authorities. A police officer observed two masked individuals fleeing the scene just before the blast. While no injuries were reported, investigators are seeking public assistance to identify the suspects captured in released photos. The FBI is also involved in the ongoing investigation.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Egypt opens $1.2B Grand Museum, showcasing Tutankhamun’s tomb in full for the first time
item.description: Egypt has opened the Grand Egyptian Museum, a massive new archaeological museum. It showcases over 100,000 artefacts spanning 7,000 years of history. The museum's biggest attraction is the full display of Tutankhamun's treasures, reunited for the first time. This grand opening aims to boost Egypt's tourism and cultural heritage.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Justin Trudeau dresses as Katy Perry’s ‘Left Shark’ for Halloween, sparking romance buzz
item.description: Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau sparked romance rumors with pop star Katy Perry by dressing as her iconic "Left Shark" for Halloween. This playful gesture followed their first public appearance in Paris. Sources reveal the pair have been dating since mid-2025, finding a strong connection after their respective high-profile breakups.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: Did Charlie Kirk predict his own murder? Candace Owens reveals eerie 'prophecy' text messages from years before his death
item.description: Shocking texts revealed by Candace Owens suggest Charlie Kirk foresaw his assassination years before his death. The late Turning Point USA founder reportedly confided in Owens about a gut feeling of being 'wiped out' and dreaming of his demise. He even compared himself to Moses, hinting at a profound, perhaps fatal, mission. Owens also alluded to internal betrayals.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Hindus realising Christian nationalists are not friends’: Mehdi Hasan weighs in on JD Vance’s remarks about wife Usha's religion
item.description: Journalist Mehdi Hasan commented on JD Vance's remarks about his Hindu wife's faith, suggesting conservative Hindus and Jews aligning with the MAGA movement are discovering Christian nationalists aren't allies. Vance's hope for his wife's conversion drew criticism, with the Hindu American Foundation urging reciprocal engagement. Vance defended his comments, calling backlash 'disgusting'.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Vivek Ramaswamy stirs row after sharing old Charlie Kirk clip; social media tells him ‘self-deport’
item.description: Vivek Ramaswamy's sharing of a Charlie Kirk video sparked controversy, with critics highlighting Kirk's past anti-immigrant remarks. The clip featured Kirk challenging a view that America was intended for 'white men of good stock,' emphasizing 'E pluribus unum.' Ramaswamy's endorsement of Kirk, despite the latter's controversial history, drew sharp criticism from many, particularly given Ramaswamy's own Indian heritage.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Viral on Instagram: US lawyer sells hot dogs in office suit amid government shutdown
item.description: As the US government shutdown continues, IRS lawyer Isaac Stein has become a viral sensation selling hot dogs in his office suit. His resourceful side hustle, born from financial strain, highlights the plight of federal workers. The story, gaining millions of views, showcases his adaptability and has sparked humorous online reactions.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Former Prince Andrew brought 40 prostitutes to hotel in Thailand using taxpayer money, reveals historian; 'spectacular fall from grace'
item.description: Royal historian Andrew Lownie alleges Prince Andrew used taxpayer-funded trips as Trade Envoy for personal gain, including claims of 40 prostitutes during a four-day Thailand visit. Lownie asserts Andrew had "no moral boundaries," turning official duties into holidays and pursuing personal business interests. He calls for transparency and for the monarchy to distance itself from the Duke.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Who was Virginia Giuffre? Epstein victim who dethroned Prince Andrew and shook the royal family
item.description: Virginia Roberts Giuffre, a survivor of Jeffrey Epstein's abuse, bravely spoke out against Prince Andrew, leading to his loss of titles and a significant blow to royal immunity. Though Giuffre tragically died before seeing the full impact, her posthumous memoir and family's continued fight ensured accountability for those in power.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Nicki Minaj thanks Donald Trump for speaking out on Christian persecution in Nigeria, but her fans aren’t happy
item.description: Nicki Minaj's praise for Donald Trump's remarks on Christian persecution in Nigeria sparked debate. While some fans accused her of aligning with the MAGA base, Minaj emphasized religious freedom and respect. Trump vowed US action, labeling Nigeria a "country of particular concern" due to ongoing violence by Islamist groups.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Sneako calls out Erika Kirk for her viral hug with JD Vance and her bold Charlie Kirk comparison
item.description: A viral video shows Erika Kirk, widow of Charlie Kirk, hugging Vice President JD Vance at a Turning Point USA event. Kirk's speech comparing Vance to her late husband sparked debate, with a subsequent hug drawing widespread online commentary. Streamer Sneako's mocking remarks added to the controversy, making the incident a major political talking point.
item.dc:creator: Sehjal Gupta

item.title: What really happened between QTCinderella and Vanillamace? The viral streamer controversy explained
item.description: A Twitch discussion about maintaining relationships with individuals holding racist or homophobic views has sparked a major controversy. Streamer QTCinderella faced backlash for her comments, leading to an emotional apology to affected communities. The incident highlights the complex balance between empathy and accountability for online personalities, prompting a wider debate within the streaming world about influence and perception.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: JD Vance’s comments on Usha’s religion raise a question: Can MAGA base accept his Hindu-Indian wife?
item.description: Senator J.D. Vance faces scrutiny over his interfaith marriage. His wish for his Hindu wife to embrace Christianity has ignited debate within the MAGA movement. This situation tests the movement's stance on religious and cultural conformity. Vance's personal life is now a public concern as he navigates this challenge with his base.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: COP30 snub: US to skip top-level presence in Brazil
item.description: The United States will not send any top officials to the COP30 climate talks, a White House official confirmed. President Trump, prioritizing fossil fuels, has withdrawn from the Paris Agreement and is rolling back climate commitments. Despite the federal government's absence, over 100 US state and local leaders are expected to attend.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Who receives SNAP? Data reveals who’s most at risk as 42 million Americans lose food aid under Trump administration
item.description: A federal government shutdown threatens food assistance for over 42 million Americans, potentially cutting or delaying Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits for November. This vital lifeline, supporting one in eight Americans, faces funding shortfalls, with states and food banks struggling to fill the unprecedented gap.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Dubai Metro to start at 3am on Sunday as Sheikh Zayed Road closes for Dubai Ride 2025
item.description: Dubai Metro extends operating hours to 3:00 am on November 2nd for Dubai Ride 2025, facilitating access for participants and spectators. Major road closures are in effect on Sheikh Zayed Road and surrounding areas from 3:00 am to 10:00 am. Salik toll fees will be adjusted to Dh6 during peak hours to manage traffic flow.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Watch: Elon Musk explains why Donald Trump is ‘not evil'
item.description: Elon Musk, speaking on The Joe Rogan Experience, described Donald Trump as "not evil" but a "product of his time," suggesting media coverage is overly harsh. Musk defended Trump's border policies, claiming strong enforcement is vital for fair elections. This comes after a public fallout and apparent reconciliation between the two figures.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: UAE health authorities urge residents aged 50+ to take shingles vaccine for protection
item.description: The UAE has launched a new vaccination drive for adults aged 50 and above. The Shingrix vaccine is now available to protect against shingles. This initiative aims to prevent the painful rash and nerve complications associated with the virus. The vaccine is accessible across all seven emirates.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk
